title: Atlanticazo march against authorization of offshore oil exploration
location: Mar del Plata Rambla/waterfront and march to the municipality; contemporaneous reports also describe rallies in other coastal cities, not fully enumerated
scope: Multi-site reports; nationally coordinated organization is not established
organizer: Self-convened residents and local environmental/social organizations; no single national organizer established
participants_original: LA NACION attributes an estimate of more than 3,000 in Mar del Plata to police; AFP and 0223 report thousands/miles without a precise count. No count is reported for other coastal cities.
threshold_50_evidence: The Mar del Plata police estimate reported by LA NACION is above 3,000. AFP and local 0223 coverage independently describe thousands/miles at the same date and location; the 50-person threshold is clearly exceeded in Mar del Plata.

occurrence.summary: Contemporaneous reports describe the completed 4 January Atlanticazo march at the Mar del Plata waterfront; AFP and 0223 also report actions in coastal cities.

start_date.summary: LA NACION and 0223 date the Mar del Plata march to 4 January 2022.

end_date.summary: The reports describe a completed same-day march/rally dated 4 January; no precise closing time or continuation beyond that date is stated.

location.summary: The documented turnout and route are at the Mar del Plata Rambla/coast toward the municipality; other coastal-city rallies are reported without a full city list.

organizer.summary: 0223 describes social/environmental groups and self-convened residents; a unified national lead is not established.

demands.summary: Protesters opposed the national offshore-exploration authorization and demanded protection of the sea; this is coded as a demand about government policy.

participants_original.summary: LA NACION reports more than 3,000 per police; Buenos Aires Times/AFP and 0223 use qualitative thousands/miles descriptions.

participants_min.summary: The only explicit numeric report is more than 3,000 in Mar del Plata; the exact count is unknown and no ceiling is published.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The LA NACION police estimate alone is well above 50; AFP and 0223 provide qualitative corroboration.

protester_violence.summary: The opened passages do not establish violence against the state; value remains unknown, not no_explicit.

state_response.summary: The opened event coverage does not describe any of the seven state-response categories; all remain unknown, not ignore.

notes: This is a high-confidence eligible Mar del Plata gathering. Other coastal-city gatherings are retained as multi-site context, not assigned the Mar del Plata attendance estimate. The demand taxonomy has no environmental category; political_behavior_process records opposition to a government authorization. No violence or state response is inferred from silence.
open_questions: Were the other coastal-city actions part of one nationally organized event or separate local gatherings?
Can additional local reports enumerate the other sites and their event-specific attendance?
Does later January reporting establish continuity after the 4 January action?

title: Self-convened agricultural producers’ assembly opposing export restrictions
location: Junction of National Routes 9 and 178 near Armstrong, Santa Fe
organizer: Self-convened producers and grassroots agricultural groups from Santa Fe and Córdoba, as reported by LA NACION
participants_original: More than 500 self-convened producers (LA NACION report); no upper count reported.
threshold_50_evidence: LA NACION reports more than 500 producers gathered at the assembly, comfortably above 50.

occurrence.summary: LA NACION reports that the public assembly took place on 8 January at the routes 9/178 junction near Armstrong.

start_date.summary: The article dates the assembly to 8 January 2022.

end_date.summary: The article describes a dated assembly on 8 January; no exact start/end time or subsequent activity is reported.

location.summary: The assembly was at the intersection of Routes 9 and 178 near Armstrong, Santa Fe.

organizer.summary: LA NACION identifies self-convened producers, base groups and organizers from Santa Fe and Córdoba.

demands.summary: Protesters opposed national-government export restrictions on beef, wheat and maize and sought producer representation for their grievances; coded as a domestic-policy choice.

participants_original.summary: LA NACION reports more than 500 self-convened producers; no exact total or ceiling is given.

participants_min.summary: The explicit lower-bound report is more than 500.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: More than 500 gathered, exceeding the threshold.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not report violence against the state; value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: No event-specific state response is reported; all seven dimensions remain unknown.

notes: The eligible assembly is supported by one opened contemporaneous body. Other results (including search-only estimates around 200 or 700 and a 2008 Infocampo tractorazo at the same intersection) are not used as 2022 counts or corroboration. Political-behavior/process is used for the national export-policy demand; category mapping remains for reviewer calibration.
open_questions: Can an independent, accessible 2022 report corroborate occurrence and the >500 count?
Do simultaneous agricultural actions elsewhere belong to this assembly or remain separate local events?
Would a reviewer prefer land_farm_issue rather than political_behavior_process for export restrictions?

title: Social-organization road and access blockades in the Buenos Aires metropolitan area
location: Several conurbano points, including Puente Pueyrredón, Puente Saavedra and Acceso Oeste at Avenida Vergara in Morón; Puente Pueyrredón was reported as the epicenter
scope: Multiple local blockades during one reported plan-of-struggle day; national coordination not established
organizer: Polo Obrero Tendencia, OCR–Resistencia Popular, Ana María Villarreal, 19 y 20 de Diciembre, Arriba los que Luchan, Organización 24 de Marzo and Bloque Obreros por el Socialismo, among the named convocants
participants_original: No numerical participant estimate reported for the six-hour blockades.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established: Página|12 reports a six-hour protest day at several sites and multiple organizations, but provides no headcount.

occurrence.summary: Página|12 reports six hours of protests and route/access cuts at multiple sites on 26 January.

start_date.summary: The article timestamp is 26 January 2022, and its text describes the six-hour action on that date.

end_date.summary: The same article describes six hours of action on 26 January; no continuation beyond that date is confirmed.

location.summary: The report names Puente Pueyrredón, Puente Saavedra, and Acceso Oeste at Avenida Vergara in Morón.

organizer.summary: The article names the organizations convening the action and quotes a Polo Obrero representative.

demands.summary: Organizers demanded promised enrollment in Potenciar Trabajo, food deliveries to community kitchens and rejection of the proposed IMF deal; coded as political/policy demands.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No participant count is stated, so the 50-person threshold remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: The opened text does not establish violence against the state; value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: The report describes earlier unmet commitments but no event-specific response across the seven dimensions; values remain unknown.

notes: A verified public action with explicit demands to national government policy is established; threshold remains open. The article calls this the first day of a plan and warns of similar action the following week, but does not confirm that later action. It is separate from the Jan27 Obelisk-to-Economy-Ministry march pending evidence of common organization or episode.
open_questions: How many people participated overall and at each site?
Were the cuts centrally coordinated as one event or several local actions?
Did the announced next-week mobilizations occur, and did the event physically close on Jan26?

title: Left-wing and Kirchnerism-aligned march against IMF debt payments
location: From the Obelisk to the Ministry of Economy by Plaza de Mayo, Buenos Aires City
organizer: Autoconvocatoria por la Suspensión del Pago e Investigación de la Deuda, Frente de Izquierda–Unidad, and allied left-wing/Kirchnerism-aligned groups, as reported by LA NACION
participants_original: No numerical estimate in the opened reports; LA NACION calls it an “enorme movilización,” and Reuters Connect caption/transcript gives no count.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established: the report’s qualitative “enorme” description and the Reuters caption do not quantify participants; no visual count was attempted.

occurrence.summary: LA NACION and Reuters Connect report a march in Buenos Aires on 27 January against IMF debt payments.

start_date.summary: LA NACION dates the march to 27 January 2022 and says it began around 10:30.

end_date.summary: LA NACION says the march ended at the Economy Ministry with a brief act on 27 January; no end time is reported.

location.summary: The procession went from the Obelisk to the Economy Ministry/Plaza de Mayo; Reuters Connect caption identifies Buenos Aires.

organizer.summary: LA NACION identifies the Autoconvocatoria for suspension/investigation of debt and the Frente de Izquierda–Unidad among groups supporting the call.

demands.summary: The march demanded suspension of near-term IMF payments and opposed repayment/renegotiation; coded as a government policy choice.

participants_original.summary: Neither opened body gives a numerical turnout. LA NACION uses the phrase “enorme movilización”; Reuters text gives no estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The 50-person threshold is not established by a numeric or sufficiently clear qualitative estimate.

protester_violence.summary: No opened passage establishes violence against the state; value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Neither opened passage describes an event-specific state response; all seven dimensions remain unknown.

notes: This is a January27 march documented separately from the February8 anti-IMF march (S024/S032/S033). No threshold or state response is inferred. The source S008 is a related search lead but body retrieval failed and is not used for event facts.
open_questions: Can another accessible contemporaneous source establish attendance of at least 50?
Does follow-up establish closure or continuity after the short act?
Can source-origin relationships for other Jan27 reports be established?

title: Boedo residents’ outage-related blockade at Avenida Boedo and Juan de Garay

organizer: Residents affected by outages; no formal organization is identified

threshold_50_evidence: Not established at this site: the qualitative “hundreds” applies across several AMBA piquetes, not the Boedo/Garay blockade alone.

occurrence.summary: Nota al Pie reports residents blocked Boedo at Juan de Garay over power outages.

start_date.summary: The article published 6 January says the Boedo/Garay blockade occurred on Wednesday 5 January 2022.

location.summary: The article identifies Avenida Boedo at Juan de Garay.

organizer.summary: Residents/neighbors are identified; no formal organization is named.

demands.summary: Residents said private providers Edesur/Edenor had failed to respond to outage complaints. A direct demand to the Argentine government or state policy is not established.

participants_original.summary: “Hundreds” refers to multiple AMBA piquetes, without a site-specific count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The cited report does not establish that 50 people gathered at Boedo/Garay.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not establish violence against the state; value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: The report mentions provider nonresponse and general ENRE measures but does not establish an event-specific state response; all dimensions remain unknown.

notes: The specific Jan5 blockade is dated, but the article describes demands mainly toward private utilities and provides only an area-wide count. General regulator measures in the same article are not linked to this action. Planned repeat activity was not verified.
open_questions: Was there a direct demand to government or regulator policy, rather than only utility service?
How many people attended this site?
Did the planned evening repeat or other named piquetes occur, and were they part of one coordinated event?

title: Residents’ electricity-outage blockade affecting access to Arana
location: Intersection of streets 137 and 90, access to Arana, La Plata area, Buenos Aires Province
organizer: Local residents/neighbors affected by prolonged outages; no named organization identified
threshold_50_evidence: Not established: the opened El Día report gives no count or crowd-size description.

occurrence.summary: El Día reports a residents’ road blockade affecting access to Arana.

start_date.summary: The report says the action took place during much of Wednesday 26 January and continued on Thursday 27 January.

location.summary: The report locates the blockade at 137 and 90, affecting access to Arana in the La Plata area.

organizer.summary: Residents/neighbors are identified; no organizing organization is named.

demands.summary: Residents connect the road blockade to prolonged outages; the direct target reported is private utility Edelap, and a demand to state policy is not established.

participants_original.summary: No participant total is reported in the accessible article portion.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No numerical or clear qualitative turnout establishes the threshold.

protester_violence.summary: Tires and branches were burned, but the report does not establish violence against the state; this field remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Edelap said it was working on a damaged transformer; that is a private-utility statement, not a coded state response. No state response is established.

notes: The article reports activity over 26–27 January and a continuing blockage on Thursday afternoon, but no physical end. Burning tires/branches is not treated as violence against the state. A separate report of employee/quintero outage complaints near Parque Pereyra does not establish a public gathering and is listed in exclusions.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people participate?
Was any demand directed to the provincial government or state oversight policy?
When did the blockade physically end, and were any state responses reported?
Did the Parque Pereyra workers gather publicly?
